components.title: Lifecycle · One order request, step by step
components.note: Illustrative order service. Press Play: the marker moves along each connection in the direction the work travels.

steps.caption: The browser posts the order. Nothing has been saved yet.
The controller saves the order, then enqueues a receipt job. It does not wait for the email.
The controller answers 201 Created while the job is still in the queue.
Later, the queue hands the job to a worker.
The mailer times out. The customer already saw success, so only the worker knows about this failure.
The worker puts the job back on the queue to try again in 30 seconds.
The second attempt reaches the mailer and the receipt is sent.

components.title: CodeMap · What the receipt change connects
components.note: Illustrative change. Select a part to read its code; switch views to compare.
components.before: The controller calls the mailer and waits for it.
components.after: The controller enqueues a job; a worker calls the mailer later.

nodes.label: Orders controller
nodes.description: After saving, enqueue delivery instead of waiting for the mailer.

nodes.label: Receipt job
nodes.description: A worker loads the saved order and calls the mailer. Timeouts retry up to three times.
nodes.code:
retry_on Net::ReadTimeout, wait: 30.seconds, attempts: 3

def perform(order_id)
  ReceiptMailer.deliver(Order.find(order_id))
end

nodes.label: Receipt mailer
nodes.description: Unchanged. It remains the only code that talks to the email provider.

components.title: CodeTour · The lines that decide the behavior

children.title: The request no longer waits for email
children.text: The illustrative change replaces a blocking call with an enqueue.
children.consequence: The response returns before delivery. A queued job does not prove the email was sent.

children.title: The job reloads the order by id
children.consequence: A retry can send a second email. Moving code into a job does not make it idempotent.
